Definition: Percentage of mobile connections using smartphones (as opposed to feature phones or basic phones). Smartphones are the minimum device requirement for accessing most digital public infrastructure services, apps, and mobile internet.
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: WATRA/ARTAO's regulatory profile of Guinea (citing ARPT/GSMA data) records smartphone penetration at 15% (2020, ~2m users), which supports a Code 1 (<20%) score. No fresher, country-specific smartphone percentage could be found despite targeted searches; GSMA's Nov 2025 Africa smartphone report and DataReportal's 2026 Guinea report (83.8% of mobile connections are 3G/4G/5G 'broadband', which is a proxy, not a direct smartphone measure) give no clear evidence of Guinea crossing the 20% threshold. Score confirmed at Code 1, but flagged for human review because the only precise figure located is five years old and no primary 2023-2025 update was found.

Value Name: Served remotely from distant regions only (>100ms latency)
Comments: Distant remote cloud availability (no local hyperscale). Assumption based on no local presence found
redteam_note: Scored >0 but NO source cited — unsupported claim, verify first. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Inflect.com's data centre directory (Sept 2025) confirms zero direct hyperscale cloud on-ramps in Guinea; AWS/Azure/GCP are reached via network interconnects to Dakar, Marseille or Lisbon, consistent with 'served remotely from distant regions'. Guinea opened a Tier 3-certified national data centre in Conakry in September 2025 (Ecofin, TechAfrica News) for hosting government data domestically, but this is a sovereign facility, not a commercial hyperscale cloud presence, so it does not change the score. Code 2 confirmed.
